summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prohibit constitutional corporations from mining thermal coal in Queensland's Galilee Basin, covering proposed mines including the Carmichael project identified in the memorandum.
Mining operations covered by the prohibition would constitute a strict liability offence, carrying a maximum penalty of two years' imprisonment, 1,000 penalty units, or both.
The area would follow the Galilee subregion boundaries in the Commonwealth's June 2018 bioregional assessment map, with the legislation commencing the day after Royal Assent.
changes: The prohibition would prevail over inconsistent laws, permits, titles and other instruments.
The law would not apply where it would acquire property otherwise than on constitutionally required just terms.
Thermal coal would be defined by its primary use in electricity generation.
summary.affected: Constitutional corporations carrying out thermal coal mining in the defined Galilee Basin area are affected.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: The speaker introduced the Galilee Basin (Coal Prohibition) Bill 2019 to prohibit thermal coal mining in Queensland's Galilee Basin, including the Adani Carmichael mine and eight other planned mines, arguing that the basin would add over 700 million tonnes of CO2 per year and that Australia must keep coal in the ground to avert climate catastrophe.
